answer: A bonded registry issues each human juror one key. Each epoch a juror signs exactly one non-transferable attestation for an agent; the ledger rejects any second agent reusing that juror and slashes the juror's bond on detection. A gale of duplicate signups requires recruiting distinct jurors, not just extra accounts. The glacier pace of finality gives auditors time to catch a juror trying to whisper the same attestation to two keys. With per-epoch reward r and juror cost c, n identities gain n(r-c), so sybils profit only while r>c; juror collusion or fake identities remain the weakness.
